meta.label: Planning window
meta.text: 1 Nov 2026 – 23 May 2027. UPSC Annual Calendar 2027 lists CSE Prelims for 23 May 2027; dates are subject to change.

meta.label: Strategy
meta.text: Nov–Dec: Mains-heavy first pass. Jan–May: Prelims-focused coverage, revision, PYQs, CSAT and mocks. Sociology weekly; Kannada/English qualifying practice.

meta.label: Study-time assumption
meta.text: 15–19 focused hours/week alongside a full-time job; adjust if your actual capacity differs.

meta.label: Source discipline
meta.text: Do not read multiple books for one topic. Choose one primary source from Source Index; use PYQs to control depth.

meta.label: How to use
meta.text: Update Daily Plan status, confidence, accuracy and backlog. Use Syllabus Checklist and Weekly Review.

meta.label: Date caution
meta.text: UPSC Annual Calendar 2027 is published. CSE notification is scheduled for 13 Jan 2027 and application deadline for 2 Feb 2027; verify the detailed notice.

meta.label: Completion rule
meta.text: A topic is complete only when you can recall it, solve PYQs/MCQs and explain mistakes.

meta.label: Official 2027 calendar dates
meta.text: CSE Prelims: 23 May 2027; notification scheduled 13 Jan 2027; last date scheduled 2 Feb 2027. Check UPSC calendar for amendments.

meta.label: Current qualifying thresholds
meta.text: CSAT Paper II: 33% minimum. Mains English and Indian-language papers: currently 25% each under UPSC guidance. Reconfirm from the 2027 detailed notification.

meta.label: Mains merit structure
meta.text: Essay 250 + GS I–IV 1,000 + Optional I–II 500 = 1,750 written merit marks; Personality Test 275. Qualifying language papers are not counted in merit.

Record definitions, processes, constitutional articles, comparisons, maps, examples, schemes, exceptions and PYQ traps. Aim for 1–2 pages per large subtopic, not copied chapters.
Start with 15–25 MCQs after a new topic; increase to 30–50 during revision. Record why wrong and guessed answers failed.

syllabus.Coverage checklist: Current events of national and international importance; History of India and Indian National Movement; Indian and World Geography – physical, social and economic; Indian Polity and Governance – Constitution, political system, Panchayati Raj, public policy, rights issues; Economic and Social Development – sustainable development, poverty, inclusion, demographics, social-sector initiatives; Environment, Ecology, Biodiversity and Climate Change; General Science.

Comprehension; interpersonal and communication skills; logical reasoning and analytical ability; decision-making and problem-solving; general mental ability; basic numeracy (Class X level); data interpretation (charts, graphs, tables, data sufficiency – Class X level).

Indian culture – art forms, literature and architecture from ancient to modern times; modern Indian history from mid-18th century; freedom struggle and contributors; post-independence consolidation/reorganisation; world history – industrial revolution, world wars, colonisation, decolonisation, political philosophies; Indian society and diversity; women, population, poverty, urbanisation; globalisation; communalism, regionalism, secularism; physical geography; distribution of resources; industrial location; geophysical phenomena.

Constitutional development, features, amendments, basic structure; Union/State functions and federalism; devolution; separation of powers; Parliament and State Legislatures; Executive and Judiciary; RPA; constitutional posts and bodies; statutory, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies; government policies; development processes; NGOs, SHGs, donors and stakeholders; welfare schemes and vulnerable sections; health, education, human resources; poverty and hunger; governance, transparency, accountability, e-governance, citizen charters, institutional measures; civil services; pressure groups and associations; India and neighbourhood; bilateral/regional/global groupings; international institutions; diaspora.

Indian economy, planning, mobilisation of resources, growth, employment, inclusive growth; government budgeting; agriculture, cropping, irrigation, storage, transport, marketing, e-technology, subsidies, MSP, PDS, food security, food processing, land reforms; liberalisation, industrial policy, infrastructure – energy, roads, railways, ports, airports; investment models; S&T developments and applications, achievements, indigenisation, IT, space, computers, robotics, nanotechnology, biotechnology, IPR; environment, conservation, degradation, EIA; disaster management; internal security, development-extremism linkages, external state/non-state actors, communication networks, media/social networks, cyber security, money laundering, border management, organised crime and terrorism.

Ethics and human interface; human values; attitude; aptitude and foundational values for civil services; emotional intelligence; moral thinkers and philosophers; public service values and ethics in public administration; probity in governance; RTI, codes of ethics/conduct, citizen charters, work culture, quality of service delivery, utilisation of public funds, corruption; case studies.

Sociology as a discipline; sociology as science; research methods and analysis; sociological thinkers; stratification and mobility; work and economic life; politics and society; religion and society; systems of kinship; social change in modern society.

Perspectives on the study of Indian society; impact of colonial rule; rural and agrarian social structure; caste system; tribes; social classes in India; systems of kinship in India; religion and society; visions of social change; rural and agrarian transformation; industrialisation and urbanisation; politics and society; social movements; population dynamics; challenges of social transformation.
Two essays; broad themes; coherent argument, examples, balanced dimensions, structure, clarity and relevance.
Kannada Paper A and English Paper B; practise comprehension, précis writing, usage/vocabulary, short essays and translation as specified in the official examination notice.
DAF; education and employment background; home state/district; hobbies; current affairs; judgement, integrity, communication and situational questions (after Mains).
